messages.subject: Re: groupComparison using multiple conditions to compare against each other?
messages.subject_clean: groupComparison using multiple conditions to compare against each other?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Matthias,

Have you figured out what you want? I am having a similar experimental design and based on your question. wanted to know if there are any interactions, I got the following response from Dr. Vitek.

"The interaction is encoded in the MSstats model directly. When you have 2 factors with 2 levels each, we in fact fit a model with 1 factor and 4 levels (i.e. all combinations of the original levels). This is equivalent to fitting a model with two factors and their interaction.

If you would like to test the hypothesis that the two factors are additive (i.e., their interaction is zero), you need to specify a particular contrast, after the model fit. If I denote Condition(1,1) the first level of the first factor and the first level of the second factor, etc, testing for the interaction being zero is equivalent to testing Condition(1,1) - Condition(1,2) - Condition(2,1) + Condition(2,2) = 0  You can specify this in the contrast function."

"You will need to specify
Comparison5 <- matrix(c(...),nrow=1)
And replace … with c(1,-1, -1,1), except that you need to change the order of the coefficients such that they correspond to Condition(1,1) - Condition(1,2) - Condition(2,1) + Condition(2,2) (I cannot do it for you since I do not know how your factors are coded)."

Hope this helps!

Priya

messages.subject: Interaction terms for a two factor and two level experimental design
messages.subject_clean: Interaction terms for a two factor and two level experimental design
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have several questions regarding my analysis of label-free proteomic data in MSstats. My experimental design has two factors, sex (male & Female), and infection status (Uninfected and infected),  with two levels within each factor and four biological replicates. I've performed contrasts for differential protein expression as per the MSstats guide and here is my code. I am also attaching my annotation file and sample of my input file.

Codes used for identifying differentially expressed proteins:
#I compared Male uninfected to male infected
comparison1<-matrix(c(-1, 1, 0, 0),nrow=1)
# Comparison of female uninfected to female infected
comparison2<-matrix(c(0, 0, -1,1),nrow=1)
#comparison of male uninfected to female uninfected
comparison3<-matrix(c(1,0,-1,0),nrow=1)
#comparison of male infected to female infected
comparison4<-matrix(c(0,1,0,-1),nrow=1)
#contrast for testing interaction between sex and infection
comparison5 <- matrix(c(1,-1,-1,1), nrow=1)

My questions are
(1) Did I make the right comparisons to test the main factors?
(2) When I perform the comparison as above, my degrees of freedom for all the comparisons are 9 which is confusing for main effects?
(3) How can I get a trellis display for all the proteins as described in Figure 3 of Clough et al 2012 <https://bmcbioinformatics.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/1471-2105-13-S16-S6>?

Could anyone please give me there insights about my concerns/questions?

Look forward to hearing from someone!

Regards
Priya
